newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac mulls live television appearance - report.
newsitem.headline: Chirac mulls live television appearance - report.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, struggling with low approval ratings in the polls, may make a live television address early next week on the topic of judicial reform, the French daily Le Monde said on Saturday.
A presidential aide had no comment on the report.
The government initiative to review judicial independence was announced by Chirac during his last live television appearance on December 12.

Questioned about a rash of sleaze probes into all of the major political parties including his own Gaullist Rally for the Republic, Chirac said he had instructed the government to name a commission to review the workings of the justice system.
Just 36 percent of the French people approved of the conserative Chirac's actions as president, according to the latest Gallup survey for the weekly L'Express, while 52 percent disapproved.
The ratings of Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe have been hard hit by public austerity policies and record unemployment of 12.7 percent.
